title: the history guard follows a cd whose target holds a quoted or escaped space
desiredOutcome: The maintainer's fix for BUG-13 (branch fix/bug-13) lands: a cd into a directory whose name holds a space, quoted or escaped, is followed, so a history rewrite of that worktree's recorded commit is judged against the worktree; nothing measured is weaker than main and no benign command is refused. SECURITY.md and the CHANGELOG say what the shared reader now resolves and what it still does not, and BUG-13 is closed with its fixing commit.

findings.issue: The class stays open in a second spelling. A cd target whose whitespace is escaped with a backslash rather than quoted still tokenizes as two words, so effective_cwd returns None (same as main, verified). In the history guard that None falls back to the payload cwd (guard-history-rewrite.py:1429-1430), which is the BUG-13 mechanism. This spelling is common because bash printf %q and tab completion produce it. The diff marks BUG-13 fixed and adds a SECURITY.md sentence that lists what remains unresolvable (expansion, glob, home shorthand, unbalanced quote) without naming this shape. Unread shape: an unquoted backslash-escaped space in a cd/pushd target.
findings.resolution: fixed in P95.1 (ceb04c89): fix task P95.1 (review-BUG13.json)
